title: Entrepreneur Flash Quiz
description: Think fast! Answer 15 rapid-fire questions about entrepreneurship, famous founders, business strategy, and startup culture. Beat the clock to prove you've got what it takes to be the next big entrepreneur!
reflection_prompt: Which founder or business idea from this quiz stuck with you, and why does it stand out?
learning_objectives: Test knowledge of famous entrepreneurs and their stories
Understand key business concepts and strategies
Learn about Indian and global startup ecosystem

how_to_play.title: How to Play
steps: Read each question about entrepreneurship, famous founders, or business strategy
Select your answer before the 15-second timer runs out
Earn 10 points for each correct answer, plus streak bonuses for consecutive correct answers
Answer all 15 rapid-fire questions to complete the quiz
Review your results to see which business topics you know best
tips: Don't overthink -- your first instinct is often correct in timed challenges
Build answer streaks for bonus points -- each consecutive correct answer adds 5 extra points
If unsure, eliminate obviously wrong options first to improve your odds

questions.question: Who is the co-founder of Infosys, one of India's largest IT companies?
What does 'MVP' stand for in the startup world?
Which company did Bhavish Aggarwal co-found?
What is 'bootstrapping' in entrepreneurship?
options: Building a company with your own money, no external funding
questions.correct_answer: Building a company with your own money, no external funding

questions.question: Flipkart was acquired by which global company in 2018?
What is a 'unicorn' in the startup ecosystem?
options: A startup valued at over $1 billion
questions.correct_answer: A startup valued at over $1 billion

questions.question: Who founded Zerodha, India's largest stock broker?
Which Indian startup became the first to be listed on both Indian and US stock exchanges?
Who is known as the 'Father of the Indian IT Industry'?
Which of these is NOT a typical stage of startup funding?
Byju Raveendran founded which famous Indian ed-tech company?
What is a 'pitch deck'?
options: A deck of playing cards for luck
A presentation used to convince investors to fund your startup
A ship's deck where deals are made
questions.correct_answer: A presentation used to convince investors to fund your startup

win_conditions.description: Answer all 15 questions correctly for maximum score! Build streaks for bonus points. 15 seconds per question — think fast!

transfer_exercises.real_world: Making fast calls during a team project deadline crunch
transfer_exercises.challenge: Practice making a decision in under 60 seconds on something you've been procrastinating. Reflect on the outcome.

transfer_exercises.game_context: Recovering from mistakes in rapid gameplay
transfer_exercises.real_world: Bouncing back after a failed presentation or test
transfer_exercises.challenge: Write down one recent failure and three specific things you learned from it.

glossary_terms.definition: The mental effort required to process information and make decisions.
glossary_terms.example: Having too many options at once makes decisions harder and slower.
glossary_terms.deep_dive: Working memory has limits. Experts chunk information into patterns, reducing cognitive load and enabling faster decisions.
glossary_terms.real_world_example: Experienced doctors diagnose faster not because they think harder, but because they recognize patterns instantly.

glossary_terms.definition: Identifying recurring structures or relationships in information.
glossary_terms.example: Noticing that certain question types always have two plausible answers helps you focus faster.
glossary_terms.deep_dive: Pattern recognition is a core skill in chess, medicine, engineering, and sport. It develops through deliberate practice.
glossary_terms.real_world_example: Air traffic controllers recognize dangerous flight patterns faster than computers because of years of pattern training.

glossary_terms.definition: The ability to direct mental attention toward what matters most and ignore distractions.
glossary_terms.example: Under time pressure, completing questions you're confident about before tackling harder ones.
glossary_terms.deep_dive: Focus is a trainable skill. The Pomodoro method, mindfulness, and deliberate practice all improve sustained attention.
glossary_terms.real_world_example: Olympic athletes train mental focus as rigorously as physical skills — pressure performance depends on it.

coaching_moment: If you get something wrong, reset and continue. Resilience isn't about never failing — it's about how quickly you get back on track.
cultural_context: India's startup ecosystem — the world's third largest — has produced over 100 unicorns. Entrepreneur Flash Quiz develops the entrepreneurial thinking that is reshaping India's economy and creating new career pathways for young Indians.
